options: It uses no keys at all
It's only used for cryptocurrency mining
The sender and receiver both use the same key to encrypt and decrypt data
It requires three or more different keys
questions.explain: Symmetric means one shared key does both jobs — encrypting and decrypting — for both parties.

questions.q: Which two real algorithms are given as examples of symmetric systems?
options: RSA and ECC
AES and DES
Bitcoin and Ethereum
SHA-256 and MD5
questions.explain: AES (Advanced Encryption Standard) and DES (Data Encryption Standard) are both real, named symmetric encryption algorithms.

questions.q: What makes asymmetric cryptography different from symmetric?
options: It doesn't use any encryption at all
It uses multiple keys — some shared, some private — rather than one key both parties share
It's identical to symmetric cryptography, just renamed
It's only theoretical and never actually implemented
questions.explain: In an asymmetric system, the sender and receiver hold different keys, unlike symmetric systems where both parties share the exact same key.

questions.q: What does RSA stand for, and what is it?
options: Rivest, Shamir, and Adleman — its creators; one of the most common public-key encryption algorithms
Really Secure Access — a wallet brand
Random Symmetric Algorithm — a type of hash function
It's not a real algorithm name
questions.explain: RSA is named directly after the three people who created it, and it's one of the most widely used asymmetric (public-key) encryption algorithms.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what actually determines a cryptographic system's real strength?
options: How new the algorithm is
Whether it's used by a famous company
The number of users on the network
Key length and complexity, not simply whether it's symmetric or asymmetric
questions.explain: While asymmetric systems are often considered more secure due to private keys, the honest measure of strength is key length and complexity, not the family it belongs to.
